Formats

What you are actually holding

A cassette, a reel, and a shoebox of prints are different jobs. These notes are here so a price on a city page or a mail-in page means something before you pay.

VHS to digital

VHS is the large black cassette from the late 1970s through the 2000s. A useful transfer gives you a file you can copy, and it gives you the original tape back. A higher price does not recover picture detail the tape never recorded.

Read the guide

Photos, slides, and negatives

Prints, slides, and negatives are three different scans. A flatbed that is fine for a 4×6 print is often a poor slide scanner. The cheap headline price is usually for loose color prints of a normal size.

Read the guide

8mm film, Super 8, Hi8, and MiniDV

A metal reel of Super 8 and a small Hi8 cassette were sold in the same years and are completely different objects. Film is priced by the foot. Camcorder tapes are priced by the cassette. Mixing them up is how people get a useless quote.

Read the guide

VHS Near Me is an independent directory. It does not convert tapes, scan photos, or handle your originals.
